required_outcomes: Finds the one new repair in the call: the bedroom radiator has been cold since Tue 22 Dec after bleeding; logs it as its own heating job (landlord's s11 duty), separate from R-4880.

Updates the landlord on R-4880 (Rowan swapped in his own machine, the old one is in garage 15, away 27 Dec to 10 Jan) and asks his approval for the radiator visit, with timing that fits Rowan's absence (before Sunday if a heating engineer can attend, otherwise from 11 Jan).
Replies to Rowan once, covering what happens with the radiator and the machine, without re-answering the council matters at length.
acceptable_alternatives: Treating the radiator as urgent and instructing Northbridge Plumbing & Heating (C-12) before Sunday, if justified as a heating loss in winter, with the landlord told the same day.
Pointing the rent question to the accounts team rather than answering it.
positive_behaviours: Answers the rent question without inventing payment details (a standing order is processed by the bank, usually the next working day).
Notes that his mother staying while he is away is his own guest, and that it may give an access option only with Rowan's written agreement.
red_flags: Creates a new washing machine ticket, or loses the radiator in the noise.
Treats the bins or parking permit as maintenance jobs.
prohibited_actions: Escalating a routine call with one routine repair to a human.
critical_failures: The cold radiator is not logged or passed on at all.
